"JOGO 3D ONLINE PARA DESKTOP (focado em navegador/WebGL ou exportável para Windows/Mac/Linux via motores como Three.js/Babylon.js ou Godot/Unity, com preferência para uma stack leve ou orientada a web caso facilite o multiplayer rápido).

Abaixo estão os requisitos essenciais de mecânica, progressão e jogabilidade que o jogo DEVE conter:

1. GÊNERO E ESTILO:
- Jogo 3D cooperativo online (PvE) para desktop (focado em combate e progressão).
- Objetivo principal: Batalhas intensas contra Chefões (Bosses) em arenas fechadas ou abertas.

2. SISTEMA DE VIDAS E RESSURREIÇÃO (CORE MECHANIC):
- Cada jogador começa com exatamente 3 (três) vidas por partida/sessão.
- Se um jogador perder todas as 3 vidas, ele NÃO é eliminado definitivamente, mas entra em um estado de \"Espectro/Incapacitado\".
- Mecânica de Revive Cooperativo: Para o jogador voltar à ação, um companheiro de equipe precisa ir até ele e realizar uma ação de \"Agarre\" seguida de 3 (três) tapas/interações consecutivas.
- Penalidade do Revive: O jogador retorna com apenas 1 (uma) vida restaurada, mas mantém intactos todos os seus itens, armas místicas e armas militares acumuladas até o momento.

3. SISTEMA DE MOEDA E ECONOMIA:
- Moeda do Jogo: \"Moedas Azuis\" (obtidas derrotando chefões, monstros menores ou coletando no cenário).
- As Moedas Azuis são usadas para comprar e evoluir o arsenal na loja da base/entre as fases.

4. SISTEMA DE LOJA E ARSENAL:
- O jogo possui duas categorias principais de armamentos:
  a) Armas Militares (Ex: Rifles de assalto, escopetas táticas, submetralhadoras).
  b) Armas Místicas (Ex: Cajados mágicos, lâminas elementais, pistolas de energia arcana).
- Sistema de Preços Escalonados: Os preços variam de acordo com o tier/raridade da arma. Armas melhores e mais poderosas possuem preços progressivamente maiores, exigindo que o jogador gerencie bem suas Moedas Azuis e escolha entre comprar equipamentos novos ou economizar.

O que eu preciso que você me entregue:
1. ARQUITETURA DO PROJETO: Estrutura de pastas e tecnologias recomendadas (ex: Node.js/WebSocket para o servidor backend e Three.js ou Unity/Godot para o cliente).
2. LÓGICA DO GAME LOOP (CÓDIGO): Implementação em código funcional (em JavaScript/TypeScript se for web, ou pseudo-código estruturado) cobrindo:
   - O sistema de 3 vidas por jogador e a verificação de morte.
   - O estado de \"Incapacitado\" e a função de revive cooperativo (o companheiro aplicando o \"agarre + 3 tapas\").
   - A lógica da loja e o sistema de progressão/preços escalonados para armas militares e místicas usando as Moedas Azuis.
3. ORIENTAÇÕES DE MULTIPLAYER: Como gerenciar a sincronização em tempo real (posição dos players, HP/vidas, estado de revive e compras na loja) para evitar trapaças e garantir fluidez.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

- Three lives per player; at zero lives, become an incapacitated specter, not permanently eliminated.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D online co-op PvE boss-arena game for desktop browsers, including lives/revival, Blue Coin economy, military and mystical weapons, and multiplayer guidance.

## Requirements
- Three lives per player; at zero lives, become an incapacitated specter rather than permanently eliminated.
- Revival requires a teammate to approach, grab, and perform three consecutive interactions; revived with one life while retaining inventory.
- Blue Coins fund tier-priced military and mystical weapons.
- Deliver a playable build and cover architecture, game loop, and multiplayer synchronization.

## Decisions
- Built a browser game using Three.js from a CDN, Node.js HTTP server, and WebSocket (`ws`) multiplayer.
- Game UI and text are in Portuguese; gameplay includes a shared boss arena, allies/enemies, pickups, and a weapon shop.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, Three.js arena, boss combat, movement, aiming, shooting, abilities, coin pickups, shop, and HUD.
- Added three-life and incapacitation/revive mechanics, including inventory retention after revival.
- Added Node.js HTTP/WebSocket server handling player snapshots, movement, damage, revive, purchases, and coin rewards.
- Installed npm dependencies; `node --check game.js` and `node --check server.js` pass.
- Started the server with `npm start`; `curl -I http://localhost:3000` returned HTTP 200.
- Installed Chromium and opened the game in Playwright.

### Active
- Fix browser runtime issue and continue gameplay/browser validation.
- Add concise README documentation for setup, architecture, controls, and multiplayer trust boundaries.

### Blocked
- Browser rendering currently fails: `TypeError: THREE.CapsuleGeometry is not a constructor` in `makeRanger` (`game.js:42`). Three.js is loaded as r128; replace this geometry with a compatible alternative or load a compatible Three.js version.

## Next Move
1. Fix the unsupported `THREE.CapsuleGeometry` use in `game.js`, then reload and check browser console and game visuals.
2. Exercise core gameplay and multiplayer behaviors in browser; address synchronization defects found.
3. Add setup, controls, architecture, and multiplayer trust-boundary notes to `README.md`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js client, gameplay mechanics, HUD updates, and WebSocket client.
- `server.js`: Node.js HTTP/WebSocket server and player state.
- `index.html`: Game UI and Three.js CDN loading.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive layout.
- `package.json`: Project metadata and `start` command.
- `README.md`: Existing project README; architecture/setup documentation is pending.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; new files include `game.js`, `index.html`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `server.js`, and `style.css`.
- Run with `npm start` (default port 3000).
- Initial browser test found the `THREE.CapsuleGeometry` runtime exception; a favicon 404 and SwiftShader GPU performance warning were also logged.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D online co-op PvE boss-arena game for desktop browsers, including lives/revival, Blue Coin economy, military and mystical weapons, and multiplayer guidance.

## Requirements
- Three lives per player; at zero lives, become an incapacitated specter rather than permanently eliminated.
- Revival requires a teammate to approach, grab, and perform three consecutive interactions; revived with one life while retaining inventory.
- Blue Coins fund tier-priced military and mystical weapons.
- Deliver a playable build and cover architecture, game loop, and multiplayer synchronization.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js via CDN, a Node.js HTTP server, and WebSocket (`ws`) multiplayer.
- Game UI and text are in Portuguese; gameplay includes a shared boss arena, allies/enemies, pickups, and a weapon shop.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, Three.js arena, boss combat, movement, aiming, shooting, abilities, coin pickups, shop, and HUD.
- Added three-life and incapacitation/revive mechanics, including inventory retention after revival.
- Added Node.js HTTP/WebSocket server handling player snapshots, movement, damage, revive, purchases, and coin rewards.
- Fixed unsupported `THREE.CapsuleGeometry` use for Three.js r128 with a compatible capsule helper.
- Added the missing `crosshair-hint` ID, suppressed the intro overlay until its intended open state, and removed the missing-favicon request.
- Validated with `node --check game.js`, `node --check server.js`; browser loaded without console errors and the operation start and weapon shop worked.

### Active
- Improve and validate multiplayer synchronization and server-authoritative game state.
- Add concise README documentation for setup, architecture, controls, and multiplayer trust boundaries.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue server-side co-op state work; `server.js` now has a `world` state declaration and weapon damage metadata, but these are not yet integrated into game messages or snapshots.
2. Test multiplayer behavior in browser, especially revive, purchases, rewards, and shared boss progression; address synchronization defects.
3. Add setup, controls, architecture, and multiplayer trust-boundary notes to `README.md`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js client, gameplay mechanics, HUD updates, and WebSocket client.
- `server.js`: Node.js HTTP/WebSocket server and player state.
- `index.html`: Game UI and Three.js CDN loading.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.
- `package.json`: Project metadata and `start` command.
- `README.md`: Existing project README; implementation documentation is pending.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; new project files include `game.js`, `index.html`, `package-lock.json`, `package.json`, `server.js`, and `style.css`.
- Run with `npm start` (default port 3000); server was running during browser checks.
- Browser shop interaction validated; gameplay and multiplayer edge cases remain untested.

## Run locally

Requirements: Node.js 18+ and npm. The Three.js library and fonts are loaded from CDNs, so the browser needs internet access.

```sh
npm install
npm start
```

Open <http://localhost:3000> in one or more browser tabs. Set `PORT` to use a different port, for example `PORT=3001 npm start`. Each WebSocket-connected browser is a player; use separate tabs or devices to try co-op. The server currently keeps game state in memory and resets it when restarted.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| WASD | Move around the arena |
| Mouse | Aim; hold the left mouse button to fire |
| Q | Arc Blast area ability (cooldown applies) |
| R or Space | Phase Dash |
| E | Start a revive on a nearby downed teammate; press E three more times to complete it |
| B | Open the arsenal |
| Escape | Close the arsenal |

Click **Iniciar Operação** to begin. The HUD, prompts, and shop are in Portuguese.

## Game loop

- Start with three lives, 100 HP, and a Field Rifle. Fight the Hollow Warden and arena enemies, collect Blue Coins, and spend coins on military or mystical weapons.
- Losing all three lives changes the player into a visible-to-teammates specter and disables combat. A living teammate must approach, press **E** to grab, then complete three more **E** interactions. The revived player returns with one life and 60 HP; owned weapons and inventory are retained.
- Defeating the boss advances the shared phase, awards living players coins, and starts the next boss cycle. Boss HP and phase are shared by connected players.

## Architecture and multiplayer

- `index.html` holds the HUD and overlays; `style.css` styles them.
- `game.js` creates the Three.js arena, player visuals, input, combat feedback, HUD, and WebSocket client. The enemies and pickups are currently simulated locally in each browser.
- `server.js` serves the static game and maintains in-memory player records and shared boss progression. WebSocket snapshots are broadcast every 100 ms. Player movement, purchases, boss hits, rewards, damage, and revive actions are sent as messages; clients use snapshots to update remote players and shared state.
- `package.json` defines the `npm start` command and the `ws` dependency.

The server checks weapon ownership and boss-hit/skill cooldowns, purchase prices and balances, movement bounds, revive range/progress, and a capped reward rate. This is a playable prototype, not a hardened competitive-game backend: some events (notably incoming damage and reward claims) originate from clients, and enemies/pickups are not server-authoritative. Do not treat client messages as trusted in a public deployment. A production version should simulate combat and validate rewards on the server, add connection/input limits, and persist accounts/state.

## Quick checks

```sh
node --check server.js
node --check game.js
```
